title: Second incompleteness and Löb's theorem

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Prove Löb's theorem and use the specified PA proof predicate to show why consistent PA cannot prove its own consistency sentence.
abstract: Can Peano arithmetic prove that none of its proofs ends in a contradiction? For the consistency sentence defined by our fixed proof checker, Gödel’s second incompleteness theorem says that it cannot, provided the system is consistent. We derive this from Löb’s theorem: when a theory with the required derivability properties proves that a sentence follows from its own provability, it already proves that sentence. Applying this to a contradiction shows why Peano arithmetic's own proof resources do not suffice to establish its consistency. A consistent extension can nevertheless assert that the original system proves a contradiction.
